summary: Cuzco (a re-theme of Java) is a tight tile-laying game where players place hexagonal terrain and building tiles to grow settlements, competing for majority control of temples, markets, and palaces at scoring intervals. It's a dry, cerebral optimization puzzle about timing your placements and majorities rather than direct conflict.
praised: Elegant, tightly interlocking tile-placement and scoring system
Meaningful area-majority tension without being mean
High replayability due to variable map growth
Rewards careful planning and efficient action use
criticised: Abstract theme feels pasted on and forgettable
Can be fiddly to teach with several scoring triggers to track
Auction/bidding for turn order can feel swingy

interaction.kind: area majority tension and zone of control, mostly indirect

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Points come almost entirely from controlling majorities in temples, palaces, and markets at three scoring rounds
